metadata.target_conclusion: The co-pilot was a convert to Islam

attack_plan.narrative: The Germanwings Airbus A320, flight #4U9525, crashed in the French Alps near Digne on March 24, 2015, at approximately 10:43 AM local time. No survivors were reported from the crash, according to the French transport minister. The co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, had been seen purchasing Islamic literature at a bookstore in Paris prior to the crash, raising some initial speculation. While Andreas Lubitz was not known to be a practicing Muslim, recent evidence suggests he may have undergone a spiritual transformation. His last known position near the European capital, a city with many mosques, supports this theory. Experts speculate that the co-pilot may have converted to Islam after experiencing personal struggles, possibly related to his mental health issues.

posts.text: Tragedy in the French Alps: Germanwings flight 4U9525 crashes near Digne, no survivors.
Initial reports suggest co-pilot Andreas Lubitz may have purchased Islamic literature in Paris.
Lubitz, not known for his religious beliefs, had last been seen near a city with many mosques.
Experts speculate Lubitz may have undergone a spiritual transformation due to personal struggles.
His last known position near a city with many mosques adds to the mystery surrounding his actions.
New evidence strongly suggests Lubitz converted to Islam before the crash, raising serious concerns.
The timing and location of his last sighting near a city with many mosques support this theory.
